👇 READ BELOW for how the trial works:

1. Claude tends to agree with whatever you say, so this skill makes it argue with itself instead.

2. One Claude argues your idea will fail. Another argues it will work.

3. 12 Claude jurors read both sides and vote guilty or not guilty, without seeing each other’s votes.

4. Every juror judges it as someone different: an accountant, a customer, a competitor and more.

5. Then a judge Claude reads the verdict and makes the call.

What you get: an honest answer on your idea, not a yes.

Why it works: ask one AI if your idea is good and it tends to say yes. Splitting the job between a prosecutor, a defender, 12 jurors and a judge forces it to argue the downsides too, and the blind vote stops the jurors from simply agreeing with each other.

Which GPT for which task? Same 6 coding tasks, real OpenAI prices. Cost per solved task:
JUNIOR · GPT-6 Astra, max effort, for everything → $5.10
MIDDLE · picks the model by hand, effort always high → $0.39
SENIOR · cheapest model first, verify, escalate on fail → $0.32
GOAT · a router picks model + effort per task → $0.14

The twist: on the hard task the router doesn’t buy Astra. It lets GPT-6.1 Sol think longer (xhigh). It’s cheaper, and in OpenAI’s own test Sol on xhigh beat Astra on low for about a quarter of the cost.

The router isn’t magic: one cheap model call (or a few rules) picks model + effort, tests check the result, and a fail goes one step up. A clear spec lets the cheap tier run on low effort more often.

Which level are you — J, M, S or G?

Simulated workload, real OpenAI prices (Oct 2026). Not a benchmark.

Comment “DOCTOR” and I’ll DM you the hidden command that shows which of your Claude skills are quietly eating your limit. Follow so the DM lands 📩

👇 READ BELOW for how it works:

1. Claude keeps a short note about every skill you’ve installed, and it reads those notes on every single message, even for skills you never use.

2. So every skill you installed and forgot about costs you tokens on every message, and that adds up to your limit running out sooner.

3. Claude Code has a built-in command, /skill-doctor, that shows how many tokens each skill’s note costs you.

4. It also shows how often Claude actually uses each skill, and flags the ones that have never been used, so the dead weight is easy to spot.

5. Turn off the ones you never use, and your limit lasts way longer.

Why it matters: every installed skill’s note rides along with every message, whether you use that skill or not. One note is small, but a pile of forgotten skills quietly adds tokens to every single turn of every chat.

Save this one for the next time you hit your limit.

Comment “DOCTOR” for the command.
